item.title: [Recap] Brandin Podziemski (GSW): Brandin Podziemski recorded a team-high 18 points (5-of-14 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds and two assists over 37 minutes to lead the Warriors to an 88-87 win over the Celtics on Sunday.
item.description:
Brandin Podziemski recorded a team-high 18 points (5-of-14 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds and two assists over 37 minutes to lead the Warriors to an 88-87 win over the Celtics on Sunday.

Podziemski helped Golden State snap a five-game losing streak in a low-scoring slugfest where both teams shot below 40 percent from the floor and failed to reach 90 points. He knocked down a clutch three-pointer to put the Warriors ahead with just over two minutes left on the clock and they managed to hold off the Celtics the rest of the way. He’ll continue to play an increased role while Stephen Curry remains sidelined with a partially-torn oblique. The Warriors have a three-game week on tap that includes matchups against the Kings, Trail Blazers and Clippers.

George Bissell

item.title: [Recap] Jayson Tatum (BOS): Jayson Tatum amassed 27 points (8-of-20 FGs, 7-of-8 FTs), 10 rebounds, six assists and one steal over 38 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Warriors.
item.description:
Jayson Tatum amassed 27 points (8-of-20 FGs, 7-of-8 FTs), 10 rebounds, six assists and one steal over 38 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Warriors.

Tatum scored 23 first-half points to pass Bill Russell for eighth place on the franchise’s all-time scoring list and keep Boston within striking distance. It wasn’t enough as he went ice-cold in the second half as the Celtics dropped their fourth straight game. He missed a critical free throw in the final minute before failing to nail a wide-open three-pointer that would’ve put the Celtics ahead in the final 30 seconds. He had a chance to deliver a game-winner following a huge steal by Hugo González, but missed a fadeaway over Draymond Green. The 28-year-old fantasy star has delivered second-round value this season, averaging 26.4 points, 6.9 rebounds, 6.7 assists, 0.7 steals and 0.7 blocks through 15 games. The Celtics have a three-game week coming up featuring showdowns against the Wizards, Hawks and Spurs.

George Bissell

item.title: [Recap] Charles Bassey (GSW): Charles Bassey chipped in 13 points (6-of-7 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), nine rebounds, three assists and three steals over 26 minutes in Sunday’s win over the Celtics.
item.description:
Charles Bassey chipped in 13 points (6-of-7 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), nine rebounds, three assists and three steals over 26 minutes in Sunday’s win over the Celtics.

Bassey delivered double-digit points for the third consecutive start shortly after Warriors head coach Steve Kerr told reporters that he wants to give Bassey an extended opportunity at center with Draymond Green moving to power forward. The decision paid dividends as Bassey came within one board of his second straight double-double. The well-traveled 26-year-old big man has looked like a viable fantasy option recently and is a worthwhile pickup in deeper formats. The Warriors have a three-game week coming up that includes matchups against the Kings, Trail Blazers and Clippers.

George Bissell

item.title: [Recap] Derrick White (BOS): Derrick White notched 14 points (6-of-21 FGs), three rebounds, five assists and one steal over 31 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Warriors.
item.description:
Derrick White notched 14 points (6-of-21 FGs), three rebounds, five assists and one steal over 31 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Warriors.

White was held scoreless in the opening half, but knocked down a couple clutch buckets in the final five minutes of regulation. He was open a couple times in the final minute but passed on those looks to feed Jayson Tatum, who missed a pair of potential go-ahead shots. He finished just 2-of-12 from three-point range and is shooting below 30 percent for the season from that range. The Celtics struggled to find secondary scoring to complement Tatum with Paul George sitting out for load management reasons on the second night of a back-to-back. The Celtics have a three-game week coming up featuring showdowns against the Wizards, Hawks and Spurs.

George Bissell

item.title: [Recap] Ivica Zubac (IND): Ivica Zubac tallied 10 points (5-of-11 FGs), 14 rebounds and one assist in Sunday’s loss to the Knicks.
item.description:
Ivica Zubac tallied 10 points (5-of-11 FGs), 14 rebounds and one assist in Sunday’s loss to the Knicks.

Zubac recorded his sixth double-double of the season on Sunday, but unfortunately, there were no defensive stats to speak of. Entering the season with a fifth-round ADP, the 7-footer’s production has underwhelmed, and he ranks outside the top-100 in nine-cat formats. Of course, Tyrese Haliburton’s hamstring injury hasn’t helped, and many of Zubac’s other Pacers teammates have been affected as well, to no one’s surprise. Getting Haliburton back, which could happen by the end of November, would be huge for all the Pacers, including Zubac.

Raphielle Johnson

Sitting just outside the top-100 in nine-cat formats, Nembhard’s current production aligns with his preseason ADP (117).

item.description:

While Tyrese Haliburton’s hamstring injury has changed the equation for the entire Pacers’ rotation, Siakam’s fantasy value has held steady. item.title: [Recap] Josh Hart (NYK): Josh Hart finished Sunday’s win over the Pacers with 10 points (5-of-11 FGs), 11 rebounds, 10 assists and one steal.
item.description:
Josh Hart finished Sunday’s win over the Pacers with 10 points (5-of-11 FGs), 11 rebounds, 10 assists and one steal.

Having struggled for much of the season’s first month, Hart needed a night like Sunday. It was a historic one: he recorded his 18th triple-double for the Knicks. That moved him into a tie for second place on the franchise’s all-time list with the late Michael Ray Richardson, and Hart trails Walt Frazier by five for the top spot. Even if the shots aren’t falling, Hart can provide solid fantasy value, which is why he’s still rostered in 79 percent of Yahoo leagues.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Bam Adebayo (MIA): Bam Adebayo recorded a triple-double with 24 points (8-of-11 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs), 15 rebounds, 12 assists, two steals and three blocks over 37 minutes, leading the Heat to a 123-113 win over the Thunder on Sunday.
item.description:
Bam Adebayo recorded a triple-double with 24 points (8-of-11 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs), 15 rebounds, 12 assists, two steals and three blocks over 37 minutes, leading the Heat to a 123-113 win over the Thunder on Sunday.

This marquee matchup lost some of its luster with generational talents Giannis Antetokounmpo (groin) and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (back, neck) both sidelined by injuries. Adebayo picked up the scoring slack with an exceptionally efficient performance, recording his ninth career triple-double, accomplishing the feat for the first time since November 29, 2024. The most impressive part of this effort was that he reached the 20-point plateau on just 11 shot attempts while earning only nine trips to the free-throw line. The Heat have a challenging three-game week ahead featuring road matchups against fellow Eastern Conference contenders in the 76ers, Knicks and Cavaliers.

George Bissell

item.title: [Recap] Jared McCain (OKC): Jared McCain posted a team-high 20 points (7-of-17 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), two rebounds and three assists over 29 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Heat.
item.description:
Jared McCain posted a team-high 20 points (7-of-17 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), two rebounds and three assists over 29 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Heat.

Oklahoma City leaned on both McCain and backcourt mate Ajay Mitchell to carry their offense with perennial MVP candidate Shai Gilgeous-Alexander sitting this one out, likely for precautionary reasons, due to back and neck issues. McCain matched a season-high with 17 field goal attempts and has scored at least 18 points in seven of his last nine games since November 6. He’s still a one-dimensional scoring threat for fantasy purposes, but his increased role with the Thunder should keep him on fantasy radar screens. The Thunder have a quick turnaround with a road tilt against the Pacers on Monday before facing the Timberwolves and Bucks to close out a three-game week.

George Bissell

item.description:
Bennett Stirtz scored a season-high 21 points (7-of-14 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds and five assists over 32 minutes off the bench in Sunday’s loss to the Heat.

Stirtz predictably saw increased opportunities off the bench spelling both Ajay Mitchell and Jared McCain with superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander sitting out with back and neck issues. He established season-high marks in points (21), minutes (32) and shot attempts (14) while also dishing out five assists. The unheralded 23-year-old is rapidly becoming a key contributor for the injury-ravaged Thunder, averaging 15 points over his last three games. The Thunder have a quick turnaround with a road tilt against the Pacers on Monday before facing the Timberwolves and Bucks to close out a three-game week.

The 24-year-old guard has played a much larger role this season for the injury-depleted Thunder than previously envisioned, averaging a career-high 28 minutes through 15 games. He’s cooled down considerably after a sizzling-hot start to the year and hasn’t reached 20 points in any of his last six games since early November. The Thunder are back in action with a road matchup against the Pacers on Monday before closing out a three-game week against the Timberwolves and Bucks.

item.title: [Recap] Darius Acuff (SAC): Darius Acuff Jr. tallied a team-high 21 points (7-of-23 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), six rebounds and eight assists over 40 minutes to lead the Kings to a 97-96 win over the Celtics.
item.description:
Darius Acuff Jr. tallied a team-high 21 points (7-of-23 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), six rebounds and eight assists over 40 minutes to lead the Kings to a 97-96 win over the Celtics.

Acuff has an extremely bright future as a dynamic, high-volume scoring machine and he’s starting to become more efficient as his rookie season progresses. He continues to have a permanent green light to attack on the offensive end of the floor and he had little trouble slashing and creating shots against some of Boston’s stronger defenders in this one. He’s still prone to the occasional defensive lapse, but that figures to get cleaned up over time. The 20-year-old lottery pick is averaging 25.4 points, 3.6 rebounds, 7.4 assists and 0.9 steals through 16 games. He’s clearly on the ascent as a fantasy contributor and looks like a potential franchise cornerstone for Sacramento to build around. item.title: [Recap] Mike Conley (BOS): Mike Conley delivered a team-high 19 points (6-of-7 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), four rebounds, two assists and three steals off the bench in Saturday’s loss to the Kings.
item.description:
Mike Conley delivered a team-high 19 points (6-of-7 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), four rebounds, two assists and three steals off the bench in Saturday’s loss to the Kings.

Things unraveled in the third quarter as Boston went 0-for-15 from three-point range and were outscored 35-13 in the frame. Conley was one of the few bright spots in this one, coming off the bench to help lead a late comeback effort that fell just short. The 39-year-old veteran saw a huge spike in minutes with Derrick White (shoulder) sitting out and Payton Pritchard struggling to get going offensively. He was a perfect 4-of-4 from three-point range and also added three steals. He’s a non-factor for fantasy purposes at this stage of his career, but he could wind up playing an important role for Boston as a steadying presence in the postseason. The Celtics have lost three straight and will close out the week with a road tilt against the Stephen Curry-less Warriors on Sunday.

item.description:

Sabonis took a backseat on the offensive end of the floor with rookie Darius Acuff Jr. doing most of the driving for Sacramento, but he was a real factor on the glass, especially in the second half when Boston’s starting center Neemias Queta was forced to the bench with foul trouble. The fact that Jayson Tatum, an outstanding rebounder in his own right, sat this one out for load management reasons also helped. He committed seven turnovers, but it didn’t end up mattering as the Kings got hot in the third quarter and managed to pick up their second win of the year. Sabonis is averaging 14.1 points, 13.6 rebounds and 5.3 assists through 15 games this season. The Kings have a three-game slate coming up with matchups against the Spurs, Warriors and Timberwolves.

They built a 13-point lead by halftime, but went ice-cold in the third quarter, which allowed Sacramento to get back into the game. item.title: [Recap] DeMar DeRozan (DEN): DeMar DeRozan provided a boost off the bench with 15 points (4-of-11 FGs), two rebounds, two assists and one steal against the Rockets on Friday.
item.description:
DeMar DeRozan provided a boost off the bench with 15 points (4-of-11 FGs), two rebounds, two assists and one steal against the Rockets on Friday.

DeRozan started this season scoring in double figures in each of Denver’s first three games. In the 10 games since, he has only scored in double figures three more times. The positive news is that he’s reached that mark in back-to-back games. DeRozan isn’t going to provide value anywhere near what he has throughout his career, but if he can continue to be a reliable bench scorer for Denver, he’ll be a valuable piece for this team when the playoffs arrive.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Victor Wembanyama (SAS): Victor Wembanyama had 32 points (13-of-26 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), 11 rebounds, three assists, one block, one steal and two three-pointers in the Spurs’ 124-112 victory over the Clippers on Thursday.
item.description:

Wembanyama had another excellent game, though he continues to struggle from behind the three-point line. The 22-year-old center is just 3-of-15 from behind the arc over his last two games. item.title: [Injury] RJ Barrett (TOR): RJ Barrett has been diagnosed with a mild right hamstring strain and will be re-evaluated in two weeks.
item.description:
RJ Barrett has been diagnosed with a mild right hamstring strain and will be re-evaluated in two weeks.

Barrett was held out of Wednesday’s loss to the Wizards after playing 39 minutes in Tuesday’s loss to the Knicks. The injury was initially diagnosed as right hamstring tightness, but the Raptors now say it’s a strain. With Barrett sidelined, the Raptors will have to rely more on Scottie Barnes and Immanuel Quickley offensively, and Jamison Battle could move into the starting lineup.

item.title: [Injury] Dylan Harper (SAS): Dylan Harper (hip) has been diagnosed with a left hip external rotator strain and is expected to miss 2-3 weeks.
item.description:
Dylan Harper (hip) has been diagnosed with a left hip external rotator strain and is expected to miss 2-3 weeks.

Harper suffered the injury in the final minute of Tuesday’s loss to the Pistons and required assistance to return to the locker room. His absence is a big deal for the Spurs, as the second-year guard has been playing well, but things could have been worse. Julian Champagnie, who can provide solid fantasy value, especially for managers needing three-pointers, should move into the starting lineup.
